title: Equality of spectral and probabilistic noise operators
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with a probability mass function $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set with decidable equality. Suppose a real orthonormal basis of functions on $\Omega$ is indexed by $\iota$, with one basis vector equal to the constant-one function and with orthonormality taken in the inner product weighted by $\pi$. For every natural number $n$, every correlation parameter $\rho\in[0,1]$, and every real-valued function on $\Omega^n$, the operator defined by weighting its product-basis Fourier coefficients by $\rho$ to the power of the number of nonconstant coordinates equals the operator that, independently at each coordinate, keeps the input with probability $\rho$ and otherwise resamples from $\pi$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite and nonempty, with decidable equality
The real function space on $\Omega$ has the specified basis, including a constant-one basis vector and the stated $\pi$-weighted orthonormality
